```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(haven)

# The clean data: one row per consenting household. The file sits next to
# this report, so there is no path to set. You don't need to change this part.
hh <- read_dta("../1-data/household-analysis.dta")
```

## Summary

<!-- STEP 4: replace ___ below (keep the quotes) with the variable for
     "chlorinated on 1+ of the past 7 days". The household count is already
     done for you. -->

This report covers **`r format(nrow(hh), big.mark = ",")` households**. **`r round(100 * mean(hh[["___"]], na.rm = TRUE), 1)`%** of them added chlorine to their drinking water on at least one day in the past week.

## Descriptives by water source

```{r descriptives, eval = FALSE}
# STEP 2: replace each ___ with a variable name, then set eval = TRUE above
hh %>%
  group_by(___) %>%                                      # water source: piped or not
  summarise(N               = n(),
            chlorinated_pct = 100 * mean(___, na.rm = TRUE),  # chlorinated, 1+ of past 7 days
            chlorine_days   = mean(___, na.rm = TRUE),        # days chlorinated
            boiled_pct      = 100 * mean(___, na.rm = TRUE),  # boiled, 1+ of past 7 days
            stored_pct      = 100 * mean(___, na.rm = TRUE),  # has water stored now
            very_safe_pct   = 100 * mean(___, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # rates water very safe
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

## Main outcome

```{r figure, eval = FALSE, fig.height = 3.5}
# STEP 3: replace each ___ with a variable name, then set eval = TRUE above
hh %>%
  group_by(___) %>%                                       # village
  summarise(chlorinated_pct = 100 * mean(___, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # chlorinated, 1+ of past 7 days
  ggplot(aes(factor(___), chlorinated_pct)) +             # village again
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Village", y = "Chlorinated, past 7 days (%)")
```
